items.followUp: Give four differences between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: A compound has a fixed composition or ratio of elements, while a mixture can have variable composition or proportions.
rubric.description: Contrasts the composition of compounds and mixtures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a compound has a fixed composition or ratio and a mixture has a variable composition or ratio.

rubric.why: The elements in a compound are chemically combined, whereas substances in a mixture are physically mixed.
rubric.description: Contrasts how compounds and mixtures are formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for contrasting chemical combination with physical mixing.

rubric.why: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements, while mixture components retain their individual properties.
rubric.description: Contrasts the properties of compounds and mixture components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for contrasting the properties of a compound with those of the components of a mixture.

rubric.why: The elements in a compound are separated by chemical methods, while mixture components can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.description: Contrasts the methods used to separate compounds and mixtures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for contrasting chemical separation with physical separation.

modelAnswer: A compound has a fixed composition and its elements are present in a fixed ratio; a mixture can have variable composition and proportions.
The elements in a compound are chemically combined; the substances in a mixture are physically mixed.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their individual properties.
The elements in a compound can be separated only by chemical methods; the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.

items.followUp: Define solubility and describe how increasing temperature affects the solubility of solids and gases in water.

rubric.why: Solubility describes the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a solvent under specified conditions.
rubric.description: States that solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying solubility as the maximum amount or quantity of solute that dissolves.

rubric.why: It is commonly expressed as the amount dissolving in 100 g of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
rubric.description: Gives the reference amount of solvent and temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning 100 g of solvent and a temperature, or equivalent specified conditions.

rubric.why: The solubility of most solid solutes in liquids generally increases as temperature rises.
rubric.description: States the general effect of increasing temperature on solid solutes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solubility of most solids generally increases with rising temperature.

rubric.why: The solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases as temperature rises.
rubric.description: States the general effect of increasing temperature on gases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas solubility in liquids generally decreases with rising temperature.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
It is commonly expressed as the amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent at a specified temperature.
As temperature increases, the solubility of most solid solutes in liquids generally increases.
In contrast, the solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases as temperature increases.

items.followUp: Define relative molecular mass and state what one atomic mass unit represents.

rubric.why: Relative atomic mass compares the average mass of an atom of an element with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.description: Defines relative atomic mass using the carbon-12 reference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the average atomic mass comparison with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

rubric.why: One atomic mass unit is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining 1 u as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

modelAnswer: Relative atomic mass (Ar) is the average mass of an atom of an element compared with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
One atomic mass unit (1 u) is one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

items.followUp: State two limitations of Rutherford's atomic model.

rubric.why: According to classical theory, revolving electrons should radiate energy, lose energy and eventually fall into the nucleus, so the model could not explain atomic stability.
rubric.description: Identifies the failure to explain atomic stability.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus, or that this leaves atomic stability unexplained.

rubric.why: Rutherford's model could not explain the line spectra of atoms or the discrete energy levels of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies the failure to explain atomic line spectra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the model could not explain atomic line spectra or discrete electron energy levels.

modelAnswer: Rutherford's model could not explain the stability of the atom: revolving electrons should radiate energy, lose energy and eventually fall into the nucleus.
It could not explain the line spectra of atoms or why electrons have discrete energy levels.
